segments.narration: Three pigeons once sat in the nose of a missile. Not as cargo. As the guidance system, pecking at a screen.
Lenses threw the target onto that screen. The bird pecks where the ship is, the screen tilts, sensors read the angle, the missile turns.
And it worked. One pigeon pecked over ten thousand times in forty-five minutes without stopping. Birds don't panic and don't get distracted.
The defence committee called it eccentric and impractical. Then handed over 25,000 dollars anyway, and cancelled the whole thing in October 1944.
The Navy quietly restarted it in 1948 as Project Orcon, and finally killed it in 1953, when electronics got reliable enough.

verdicts.claim: In B.F. Skinner's Project Pigeon, one to three trained pigeons rode in a missile's nose cone and pecked at a projected image of the target to steer it.
